683	## Performance Implications
684	- **CPU (all UNVERIFIED on a release export; S1/S3 pending)**: a typed getter is one method call plus an element read; the presentation read side per frame is a handful of getters and, once per Graph step, one `failures()` scan over `count` rows. Phase loops iterate ascending slots over local column aliases (probe: a read-modify-write loop over 4096 elements costs 58.7 microseconds in the debug editor, about 14 ns per element). Division through `IntMath.floor_div` is about 12 times a bare operator (ADR-0005 P14, editor); S1 decides whether that is inlined in named hot files. `snapshot` builds about 70 `duplicate()` entries and a few nested Dictionaries; `duplicate()` is deferred copy-on-write (0.11 microseconds per 4096-element column) and the **first write to each column after a snapshot pays the copy** (0.71 microseconds per 32 KB column, probed), so the cost lands on the first mutators after a save, not on the snapshot. Restore validation is a linear pass over about 70 columns and 600 rows (tens of thousands of element checks, estimated 0.2 to 0.5 ms in the editor, inside ADR-0012's 2 ms with `post_restore`).
685	- **Memory**: persisted columns at the MVP roster are about 25 KB (the payload size); at the capacity ceilings (`MAX_GRAPH_NODES` and `MAX_GRAPH_EDGES` slots) about 0.35 MB of node columns and 0.6 MB of edge columns plus ports; caches and scratch are of the same order, so the whole block is estimated at a few MB at capacity and well under 1 MB at MVP. ESTIMATE; the kernel's joint memory assertion (CR-17) is the check.
686	- **Load Time**: restore validation and cache rebuild are linear in rows; type tables and `GraphTuning` load in stage 1 of the content loader (ADR-0007).
687	- **Network**: none at MVP; `SHARED_SUMMARY` (VS-B, ADR-0032) reads the same columns and is at most 1 KB.
688	
689	## Migration Plan
690	There is no Graph code yet. Implementation order: (1) `src/shared/graph/` pure files and `GraphTuning` (loader stage 1) with their boot tests; (2) `GraphState`/`GraphCaches`/`GraphScratch`/`GraphDiag`, `GraphSchema`, `GraphSnapshot` and the reflection and schema-fingerprint tests; (3) `GraphFaults`, `GraphFault`, `GraphRestore` with the fuzz corpus; (4) M1 and `ensure_derived`; (5) the rest of the mutators and the view. The foundation asks and GDD syncs below land before the first story that depends on them. No existing code or save format is migrated.
691	
692	## Validation Criteria
693	- **Schema**: `GraphSchema` columns equal the payload keys of a populated state; the committed fingerprint changes only with `schema_version`; every column has a min, max, type and canonical-zero predicate.
694	- **Reflection and zero-and-diff** (§ 6.3) pass on `GraphState`, `GraphCaches` and `GraphScratch`; `derived_members.json` is exact.
695	- **Round trip**: `snapshot(restore(snapshot()))` is canonical-byte identical, tombstones included, at ticks T..T+5 and mid-fault; `block_hash` twice with no `open_for` hits the cache.
696	- **Restore fuzz**: 1,000 seeded mutations classified V/I/B; every I yields exactly the reason of its row in § 7.2; the live block is byte-identical before and after each failure; a store above a lowered live cap restores exactly and is reconciled in the first phase 0 with `stock_clamped` 1 and `saturations` all zero.
697	- **Size**: the F-MVP fixture (105 nodes, 150 edges) snapshots to at most 32 KB; the per-table bytes match § 3.
698	- **Conservation**: all four totals equal their instantiation baseline after every step of every fixture; `saturations` all zeros.
699	- **Ids**: counters never decrease across weld, cut, discard, restore; no id is reused (property test over random mutator sequences); `ids.lock.json` agrees with `GraphIds`; a stale id no-ops/rejects for every mutator.
700	- **Overflow**: a tuning with `GAS_SCALE` raised refuses at boot naming the operand pair; a fixture at every field maximum matches an arbitrary-precision oracle.
701	- **Purity and independence**: every `GraphView` getter leaves `state_hash` unchanged; the Perception-block fixture of LS-22 gives an identical `state_hash`.
702	- **Keys**: a per-mutator fixture in a fresh kernel asserts each mutator's discrete changes mark exactly the declared kinds and ids.
703	- **Lints** (once ADR-0010 accepts them): OWN-01, READ-03 token list for the six owned constants, SIM-03/04/05, HOT-01 on the phase functions, each with bad and good fixtures (FIX-01).
704	- **Engine**: probes (a) to (i) re-run on a `template_release` export; S0-a/S0-b, S1, S3 recorded.

### 1. One step, three hooks, three cursors (TR-lsg-008)

A **step** is the unit of Graph time. `step_no = IntMath.floor_div(clock.tick(), tuning.graph_step_ticks)` for all three hooks (`GRAPH_STEP_TICKS`, the same constant as the hooks' divisor). The three hooks of step *n* run on ticks `6n + o_power`, `6n + o_atmo` and `6n + o_failure` with the offsets 0, 2 and 4. The offsets are data in `GraphTuning` (`hook_offset_power`, `hook_offset_atmo`, `hook_offset_failure`), so the GDD's data-only revert (all three 0) is a data change. A boot check (`GRAPH_BOOT_TUNING`, ADR-0011 § 8.4) requires the offsets to be non-decreasing and each at most `graph_step_ticks - 2`; the second rule makes `step_no` identical whether `ClockView.tick()` inside P3 names the executing tick or the next one (KRN-LAT-02 has not yet said which), because `floor_div(6n + o + 1, 6)` equals `n` for every `o <= 4`.

| Hook id | Offset | `after` | Phases | Cursor written at the end |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `graph.propagate.power` | `hook_offset_power` (0) | none | 0 to 3 | `last_step_power` |
| `graph.propagate.atmo` | `hook_offset_atmo` (2) | `{id: graph.propagate.power, tolerates_stale: true}` | 4 to 7 | `last_step_atmo` |
| `graph.propagate.failure` | `hook_offset_failure` (4) | `{id: graph.propagate.atmo, tolerates_stale: true}` | 8 to 11 | `last_step_failure` and `last_step_no` |

The two edges fix the resolved order (power, then atmo, then failure) even though the hooks never run on one tick at the baseline offsets; `tolerates_stale` is declared on both so the kernel's boot warning list stays empty (ADR-0003 § 8 check 3). The Graph registers the three descriptors consecutively, power first, so registration index agrees with the edges. Dependents name the hook they read: Suit's `suit.vitals` is `after: graph.propagate.atmo` at the same offset, Attention is `after: graph.propagate.power`, Emitter State's `emitter.place` is `after: graph.propagate.failure` (all registered by their owners, architecture hook schedule).

**Cursor semantics.** `last_step_X` is the `step_no` of the last completed run of hook X. `last_step_no` is the last **complete** step, written by the failure hook at its end. This is the GDD's definition (LS-8); ADR-0011 § 2.3 words it as "the last step whose power hook completed", which is a different number for ticks 6n+0 to 6n+3, and this ADR sides with the GDD because the readers that compare it (Failure & Trail's poll cache, FT-15) want a step whose descriptors have been emitted (cross-ADR assumption on ADR-0011). A run applies a guard before any write: `step_no < last_step_X`, or `step_no == last_step_X` with `step_no > 0`, is a defect (the clock moved backwards or the hook ran twice) and raises `GraphFaults.HOOK_CURSOR` (a new local code, cross-ADR assumption on ADR-0011 § 8.1). Step 0 is the one exception, because a fresh block holds all cursors at 0 and cannot tell "step 0 not yet run" from "step 0 done". A step that did not happen (the kernel never drops a tick at `LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS` 0, and a longer stall delays ticks without skipping them) leaves a gap between cursors and is **not** repaired: the Graph never catches up and never runs a step twice (TR-lsg-007).

**The hook skeleton** (the same for all three; `hook_power` shown):

```gdscript
# src/sim/graph/graph_module.gd (additions; ADR-0011 § Key Interfaces holds the rest)
func hook_power(views: SimViews, scope: WriteScope, ctx: HookContext) -> CompletionToken:
	if not scope.open_for(GraphModule.BLOCK_ID):
		return ctx.complete()                                  # REFUSED: the kernel counts it; nothing written
	var step_no: int = IntMath.floor_div(_clock.tick(), _tuning.graph_step_ticks)
	if GraphPropagate.enter(scope, _state, _caches, _diag, GraphPropagate.HOOK_POWER, step_no) != MutatorStatus.OK:
		return ctx.complete()                                  # cursor defect: scope already faulted
	GraphPropagate.run_power(_state, _caches, _scratch, _diag, _tuning, step_no, scope, _work)
	return ctx.complete()
```

`GraphPropagate.enter` performs the cursor guard, the head-of-hook topology guard (§ 4) and nothing else; `run_power` runs phases 0 to 3 and, after each phase, returns early if `scope.faulted` (a structural fault closes the scope, ADR-0003 § 5, and the partial writes stay for the diagnostic dump); the last statement of `run_*` writes the cursor. A hook never reads a wall clock, never calls another owner's mutator, never submits a command and never allocates in steady state.

An EMPTY block (no sections instantiated, or `default_state`) runs the hooks over empty active lists: they cost nothing and the cursors still advance, so a later `INIT` or restore finds them consistent with `T`.

======
### 3. One pass: three write disciplines (TR-lsg-007, TR-lsg-032)

A **pass** is one traversal in ascending slot order over a loop's active list in which no element reads a value written by another element of the same phase. The GDD's phrase "Jacobi from a double-buffered start-of-phase snapshot" is made exact by three disciplines, and every column a phase writes is declared with one of them in the phase's doc comment (a reviewer and a test can check the declaration against the code):

- **JAC (Jacobi).** Every element reads only start-of-phase values and writes only into a `GraphScratch` accumulator; the accumulators are applied to the live column in one ascending loop at the end of the phase (`col[i] += acc[i]; acc[i] = 0`). Used by the gas exchange (phase 6 plus phase 4's room deltas), the heat input (phases 5 and 7). Because the live column is untouched until the apply, it *is* the start-of-phase snapshot, so there is no copy and no swap.
- **ALLOC (ordered allocation).** A shared quantity (an island's supply, a tank pool, a reservoir's level, the spread budget) is allocated to claimants in ascending id order against a running balance; each claimant reads only the balance and its own row. Used by the power solve, fuel, the O2 pool, reservoir leaks, the draw queue and cascades. This is a single sequential pass, not iteration.
- **OWN (own-row).** An element reads and writes only its own row and values no other element writes in the phase. Used by damage, state evaluation, `t_cool`, queue application to a named subject.

**Why accumulators, not `next` columns (a refinement of ADR-0011 § 6.2 (4) and LS-1 (j)).** A `next` column per field needs a full copy before the pass (every untouched row must be carried over) and a swap after; probe (e) shows the dense case costs about half of the accumulate-and-apply form, so speed does not decide it. Three other things do. The exchange flux is pairwise (one `Δn` is subtracted from one room and added to another), so an accumulator makes conservation visible in one place: the sum of the accumulator is zero by construction apart from the `vented` term, and a test asserts it per run. The accumulator form touches only the rows with a flux, which keeps VS-A quiescence (a section with every flux zero) a pure skip. And the persisted column is never aliased across a kernel call, so no snapshot can capture a half-swapped column. The swap-by-reference rule of ADR-0011 stays available for any future field that is rewritten wholesale; none exists at MVP, so `GraphScratch` holds accumulators only (cross-ADR assumption on ADR-0011 § 6.2).

**The scratch inventory** (all `GraphScratch`, sized by `GraphCaches.size_scratch()` in every structural mutator and in `post_restore`, never in a phase; each is all-zero at every hook exit, asserted in tests):

| Member | Type | Rows | Phase (fill / apply) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `acc_n_o2`, `acc_n_inert` | `PackedInt64Array` | compartments | 4, 6 / 6 |
| `acc_q` | `PackedInt64Array` | compartments (dJ) | 5, 7 / 7 |
| `acc_vent_mgu` | `PackedInt64Array` | sections | 6 / 6 (folded into `vented_mgu` at the apply) |
| `island_*` (supply, demand, battery draw, charge, root) | `PackedInt32Array` / `PackedInt64Array` | power components | 2 |
| `cand_slot`, `cand_mode` | `PackedInt32Array` / `PackedByteArray` | nodes + edges (candidate list) | 9 / 10 |
| `q_key` | `PackedInt64Array` | longest queue | 0 (drain sort) |
| `stack`, `queue` | `PackedInt32Array` | nodes (iterative traversals, § 4) | 1 |

**The equalisation flux (TR-lsg-032).** The gas flux across one opening is the D.1 formula and nothing else; it is a pure function in `graph_rules.gd` so the Item DB lints, `can_join` and the phase call the same code:

### 11. Hook products and restore equivalence (a finding of this ADR)

**The problem.** The kernel may snapshot on any tick (ADR-0003 § 8, ADR-0006), and the three hooks of a step are spread over ticks 6n+0, 6n+2 and 6n+4, so a restore can land between any two of them. A restored run must evolve exactly like the uninterrupted run (that is the point of persisting the queues, the cursors and the hysteresis memory). A *derived cache* is safe only if `post_restore` can rebuild exactly the value the uninterrupted run holds at that tick. LS-21 and ADR-0011 § 6.1 classify `served_pm` as derived, "because phase 2 recomputes it before use"; that is true for phase 2 of the next step, but the atmo hook, the failure hook and other blocks read it earlier, and the post-phase state no longer reproduces it: phase 2 has debited the batteries (the availability `D` of D.6 changes in the last step before a cell empties), the room temperature has moved (the heater's thermostat duty), a cable may have failed in phase 9, and a throttle may have changed (M10). A restore at 6n+3 would then feed phase 8 a different cable load or a different `served_pm` than the uninterrupted run, and the two runs would diverge in `hp` by one step's damage.

**The enumeration.** For every phase of the atmo and failure hooks, every input that an earlier phase of a *different* hook of the same step wrote, or that another block reads between hooks, classified:

| Value | Written by | Read by | Rule here |
|---|---|---|---|
| `served` (consumer satisfaction, permille) | phase 2 | phases 4, 5, 7, 8, 9; Emitter, Suit, Interaction, Instruments | **PERSISTED** (new node column `n_served`) |
| `draw` (power actually delivered to a consumer, dJ per step) | phase 2 | phases 5 and 7 (machine waste heat), 8 (HEATER `run_pm` for duty wear) | **PERSISTED** (new node column `n_draw`) |
| cable net load (W) | phase 2 | phase 8 (`ρ`, overload) | **PERSISTED** in the existing edge column `e0` for kind CABLE (the overlay is free there; ADR-0011 § 3.4) |
| reactor `out_w`, battery and tank `stock`, `fuel_rem`, `t_cool`, `tc_rem` | phases 2 to 5 | later hooks | already PERSISTED |
| island has a live source (`S + D > 0`) | derived from `out_w` and `stock` | phase 8 short burn, phase 9 SHORT | **RECOMPUTED AT CONSUMPTION** in phase 8 from persisted state (§ 8.1); not a cache |
| `circ`, `Q_cap`, `T_mach` (D.8) | phase 5 | phase 9 OVERHEAT and HOT, phase 11 | **RECOMPUTED AT CONSUMPTION** by `derive_t_mach(slot)` in phase 9 from the current persisted `t`, `t_cool`, level, `hp` and `n_served`; phase 5 uses its own local value for the heat it injects. Phase 9 therefore sees the room temperature of phase 7, one phase later than the GDD's phase-5 proxy (`gdd_sync`) |
| `P`, `p_o2`, `o2_pm`, trend | phase 7 (and `post_restore`) | everyone | pure function of `n`, `V` and the persisted `p_prev`: DERIVED, exact |
| bands, warn trackers, `p_prev` | phase 7 and 9 | phase 9, phase 11 | already PERSISTED (hysteresis memory) |
| `isolated_at`, `mode_key`, `mode_since`, `warn_since`, `fail_since` | phase 9 | phase 8 of the next step | already PERSISTED |
| `forced_next` | phase 10 | phase 0 of the next step | already PERSISTED |
| topology caches | `ensure_derived` | all | DERIVED; rebuilt from persisted connectivity state; equal at every hook head by § 4 |
| accumulators | phases 4 to 7 | within one hook | SCRATCH, zero at every hook exit |
| descriptor store, alarm list, loop summaries, last-emitted buckets | phase 11, phases 2 to 5 | Failure & Trail (presentation), **Emitter State fault glow (sim)**, Attention, Suit | DERIVED, re-derived in `post_restore`; may differ from the uninterrupted value **until the next phase 11 or next producing phase** when state moved since (window below); the last-emitted buckets are seeded from the restored values (ADR-0011 § 7.4 (4)) |
| `power_use` window (`delta_w_last5`) | phase 2 | Attention | seeded **flat** by `post_restore` (the GDD's rule; an accepted divergence, bounded to five steps of Attention's stimulus, ADR-0022 decides whether it matters) |

**Decision.** Two node columns, `n_served` and `n_draw` (`int32`, written by phase 2 only and zero for every node that is not a power consumer, canonical zero), and an edge overlay (`e0` of a CABLE is its net load), become **persisted hook products**. Everything else in the table is persisted already, recomputed at its single point of consumption from persisted state, or accepted as a re-derived cache with a stated window. `run_pm` for a HEATER is `IntMath.floor_div(1000 x n_draw, maxi(1, req))` (the GDD's `floor(duty_t x served_pm / 1000)` without a separately stored `duty_t`); for every other consumer it stays `n_served` while `req > 0`, and the REACTOR's stays `floor(1000 x out_w / out_w_rated)` (GDD LS-19, `gdd_sync`). `GraphView.served_pm(id)` reads the persisted column.

**What this costs in the data model (a request to ADR-0011, not a unilateral change):** `n_served` and `n_draw` move `served_pm` out of the DERIVED class (ADR-0011 § 6.1, § 7.4 (3), Alternative 7, LS-21, TR-lsg-004 wording); `derived_members.json` loses `served_pm` and the schema fingerprint and `GraphSchema` gain two columns with the usual range and canonical-zero predicates; the F-MVP size grows by 8 bytes per node row, about **840 bytes at 105 nodes: from the probed 29,674 canonical bytes to about 30,514 against the 32 KB ceiling of TR-lsg-036, headroom from about 7 percent to about 4.6 percent**. ADR-0011 § 3.11 lever 1 (moving `thaw_until`, `isolated_at` and the non-fluid stamps into a side table, about 1.8 KB) restores about 10 percent and is the first lever if S3 measures above 31 KB. The alternatives (Alternatives 4 and 5 below) were to re-derive everything and accept the divergence, or to make every cache live-derived.

**What stays a window.** The descriptor store, the alarm list and the loop summaries are not persisted. In the uninterrupted run they hold the value **as of the last phase 11** (or the last producing phase); after a restore they hold the value **as of the restore tick**. They differ whenever Graph state moved in between (phases 0 to 7 of the current step and any mutator since the last phase 11), and the next phase 11 repairs the difference, so the window is at most one step (`GRAPH_STEP_TICKS - 1` ticks). Making them exact would mean rebuilding the store after every hook and every mutator (three O(subjects) rebuilds per step plus one per M13 resubmit), which costs more than the window is worth (Alternative 5). Their sim-visible reader is Emitter State's fault glow (`emitter.place`, every tick, ordered after the failure hook); their other readers are presentation. ADR-0017 decides whether fault-glow hysteresis makes the window insensitive; this ADR guarantees only that it is bounded by one step and measures it with RE-2.

**Tests (Validation).** *RE-1 (Graph persisted state):* for each restore tick *t* in a full 12-tick window across the fixture set (HEALTHY, PWR-OVL, the thaw window, a pending draw, a dormant derelict), snapshot at *t*, restore into a fresh kernel, and run to the end of the second failure hook after *t*: the `graph.state` block hash equals the uninterrupted run's at every tick from the first failure hook after *t* onward. *RE-2 (downstream):* the same run compares `state_hash` over every SIM block and reports, per block, the first divergent tick; any divergence outside the window above fails. *RE-3 (determinism):* two restores of the same bytes with the same epoch and commands give identical hashes at every tick. If ADR-0011 declines the columns, RE-1 weakens to "equal from the next power hook after the restore except at the enumerated boundary cases", and the three boundary cases (battery final step, thermostat flip, cable failure between hooks) are listed as known divergences in the Graph epic; the design above is the recommended resolution.

=====
### 4. Topology refresh and derived caches (TR-lsg-010, TR-assembly-034)

**One function, three call sites.** `GraphDerived.ensure_derived(...)` is the single idempotent rebuild of every topology-dependent cache; it returns at once while `caches.topo_dirty` is clear. It is called (a) at the end of **every structural mutator** (M1 to M6, M8, M9, M19) and in `post_restore`, so a weld, cut, discard, install or valve flip is complete, with its caches, when the mutator returns (the weld-preview drag and `can_join` never pay a rebuild, and no hook can interleave with a mutator because the kernel is single-threaded); (b) at the **end of phase 9** when a phase-driven state change altered connectivity (a CABLE, CABLE_JUNCTION, PIPE, DUCT or VALVE crossing the FAILED boundary, or a DESTROYED subject), so phases 10 and 11 (the descriptor store, the alarm list) and every reader after the failure hook see the split islands, and the power hook of the next step solves them (C1, D.15 BROKEN-BREAKER: "on run 1 the island splits"); and (c) as the **head guard** of all three hooks (`GraphPropagate.enter`), which is the GDD's "at the head of whichever Graph hook first runs after a structural mutator". Because (a) and (b) rebuild before control leaves the writer, `topo_dirty` is never left set across a tick boundary in a correct build, so a `GraphView` call to `ensure_derived()` (ADR-0011 § 9.1) is always the no-op guard it is documented to be and **no read ever pays a rebuild in an arbitrary presentation frame** (LS-19). The head guard is therefore **defect-only**: a hook that finds `topo_dirty` set has met a writer that forgot its rebuild; the guard still rebuilds (so the run is correct) and increments `GraphDiag.late_rebuilds`, which every Graph test asserts is zero. A view-side rebuild must not clear the flag silently: `GraphView` calls the same function and the same counter, so a rebuild outside a writer is never masked.

**What `ensure_derived` builds**, in this order, all into preallocated `GraphCaches` members sized by `size_derived()` (structural mutators and `post_restore` size them; the hook path never resizes): the four id-to-slot maps and the edge endpoint slots (ADR-0011 § 4.2); the **active lists** `active_nodes`, `active_edges`, `active_comps`, `active_seams` (ascending slot, tombstones and dormant sections excluded, § 10), the typed sublists `store_slots` and `machine_slots`, and `exchange_links` (the stored OPENINGs, hull holes and seam weeps phase 6 walks); `V` and `exposed_tiles` per compartment through `RoomSource`; the adjacency CSR; the loop **components** for loops 1 to 4 and, for POWER, the **trees** and `path_cap`; the POWER island list; and the sizes of the scratch and the descriptor store. `degrees` and `deg_max` are **not** cached: an OPENING counts toward a room's degree only while its `area` is above 0 and a hull segment only while it has a hole, and both change without a structural mutator (M13, a phase-9 breach), so phase 6 recomputes them in one O(E) pass at its head into scratch (a refinement of LS-8's phase 1; `gdd_sync`).

**Connectivity predicate (the one definition).** An edge joins its two endpoints in a loop's component only if: a VALVE is open; a CABLE or seam cable has `state` not FAILED/DESTROYED (its `cap` is positive); a PIPE, DUCT or FUEL PIPE has `state` not FAILED/DESTROYED; a CABLE_JUNCTION has its breaker closed; and a port is not CAPPED or OPEN_END for flow purposes. OPENINGs are the atmosphere's exchange links, not loop topology, and do not enter components. This single predicate is why TR-boarding-041 holds without a special case: an uncapped stub of a cut derelict leaks from the pool of **its own component**, which includes the home network's pool only while the seam VALVE is open, because a closed valve splits the component.

**Algorithm.** Components are found by an iterative breadth-first traversal over `active_nodes` in ascending slot with a preallocated `stack`/`queue` in `GraphScratch`: the first unvisited node found is the lowest id of its component, so the root is the lowest id by construction; POWER trees take parent pointers and a BFS order, and tree flow is accumulated by walking that order in reverse. No function is recursive, and a POWER cycle found here (R12 forbids them; `POWER_CYCLE` rejects them at M1 and `can_join`) is `GraphFaults.STRUCT_CSR`. Cost is O(N + E), measured in S1; if the eager rebuild breaks the placeholder budgets of `weld_join` and `cut_detach` (the structural entry points of the GDD's S1 criterion), the lever is to rebuild only the loops named in a per-loop dirty mask, which changes no result.

====
### 8. Endogenous damage, randomness, cascades and onsets (TR-lsg-011, TR-lsg-012, TR-derelict-011, TR-derelict-037, TR-ftrail-038)

**8.1 Damage (phase 8).** One pass over `active_edges` then `active_nodes` in ascending slot, OWN writes only. Each subject's loss is the D.9 sum `Δhp = IntMath.floor_div((Δovl + Δwear + Δshort) x rate_pm x stress_pm, 1000000)` with the product bounded by D.13, passed through `gate_floor` and `apply_loss` (§ 7) and then through the thaw and patch rules. Decisions this ADR adds to D.9:

- **`rate_pm` and `stress_pm` scale endogenous `hp` loss and nothing else.** `rate_pm` is read only in `phase_damage.gd` (a repository test greps for it, ADR-0010 `READ-03`-style, with a bad fixture): gas exchange, heat conduction and supply never see it, which is the GDD's "the breach rhythm makes the ship fail faster, not leak faster". `rate_pm` is set once, by M1: `1000` for a HOME section, `IntMath.floor_div(1000000, tuning.derelict_fault_compression)` for a DERELICT (`DERELICT_FAULT_COMPRESSION`, giving the doubled wear of TR-derelict-011) and persisted in the sections table. Clocks set by a stock draining (a tank emptying, a pool venting) do not pass through it, so the FUEL-DRIP and O2-SHIP clocks do not compress. The stress multiplier is `stress_pm` while `step_no < stress_until`, else 1000.
- **Leak wear is gated on the persisted isolation stamp (TR-derelict-037).** A subject in LEAK takes `LEAK_WEAR_BP_PER_100` only while its `isolated_at` stamp is 0, that is, while phase 9 of an earlier run has not found it isolated by a closed valve; behind a closed valve the stamp is non-zero, wear is skipped, `hp` is held and the leak resumes from the stored `hp` when the valve reopens. The GDD words the test as "descriptor `intensity_pm` > 0"; the descriptor store is rebuilt in phase 11, after phase 8, so the persisted stamp is the same fact in a form phase 8 can read and a restore reproduces. A seam weep at `hp` above `LEAK_HP` carries no LEAK wear (D.9). The dependent authored-staging tests (Derelict Authoring's closed-valve fixtures) fail if this rule changes, which is the TR's requirement.
- **"Dead" faults emit `intensity_pm` 0 until reached (TR-derelict-011).** A derelict subject authored at or below `HP_FAIL` with a powered-off module has no flow, no served power and no coolant, so every flow-fraction descriptor it owns evaluates to intensity 0 and the descriptor is emitted with a large `since_steps`; nothing special-cases it, and it wakes when a solve or a leak reaches it.
- **Short burn and the island test.** A FAILED cable in SHORT keeps burning only while an island at either end holds a live source. That test is evaluated in phase 8 from the **persisted** `out_w` of the sources and `stock` of the batteries in the cable's component (one O(islands) pass into `x.island_alive` at the head of phase 8), not from a phase-2 cache, so a restore reproduces it (§ 11; a `gdd_sync` item rewords LS-11's "this run's phase-2 result").
- **The peak and the `INRUSH_STEPS` tag.** Overload damage within `INRUSH_STEPS` of the branch's `energised_at` is tagged EXOGENOUS (a breaker closed onto an overload is a player verb); after the window the same overload is ENDOGENOUS and gated.

**8.2 Randomness (phase 8 and phase 9).** The Graph registers one **plain** stream at `BOOTING`, `graph.fail`, through `ModuleFacet.rng` (ADR-0005 § 2.3, `epoch_keyed = false`), and draws through `RngFacet.draw(stream, counter)`. The counter is an owner-defined non-negative 63-bit key:

```gdscript
# src/shared/graph/graph_rules.gd
const RNG_NODE: int = 0
const RNG_EDGE: int = 1
const RNG_COMP: int = 2                       # reserved: spark ignition (VS-A)
## 20-bit subject key: 2-bit kind, 18-bit id. Node and edge ids overlap numerically; the kind bits keep their draws apart.
static func rng_subject(kind: int, id: int) -> int:
	return (kind << 18) | id                  # id < 2^18, asserted at boot against MAX_GRAPH_NODES and MAX_GRAPH_EDGES
static func rng_counter(step_no: int, kind: int, id: int) -> int:
	return (step_no << 20) | rng_subject(kind, id)       # step_no < STEP_STAMP_MAX (2^30), so the key stays below 2^50
## Burst test: a pure integer comparison; no float, no bare modulo.
static func burst_hit(raw: int, burst_p_pm: int) -> bool:
	return IntMath.posmod_i(raw & 0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF, 1000) < burst_p_pm
```

The 18-bit id field is a decision: the largest id the Graph can allocate before the MVP's no-compaction rule makes it a slot count is `MAX_GRAPH_EDGES`, far below 2^18, and the 2-bit kind field leaves room for the VS-A compartment-keyed spark ignition. It fixes ADR-0011 Risk 7 (a thaw roll for node 5 and for edge 5 drew the same value) and keeps the GDD's `(step_no << 20) | subject` form, so the golden vectors of ADR-0005 stay valid as pure-function vectors (`GRAPH_BOOT_TUNING` asserts both caps below 2^18). ADR-0005 § 2.4 already allows "any owner-defined 63-bit key", so no Foundation change is needed. The draw is a pure function of `(world_seed, step_no, kind, id)`: it reads **no** restore epoch, so a reload replays the identical roll at the identical step (user ruling D16/X8), and it is unaffected by weld, cut, restore or content added elsewhere. Draws are not counted or stored; there is no counter to persist.

### 6. Sockets, seams and the mating predicate

- **A socket is a pre-declared attachment site** `{socket_key, facing N|E|S|W, line_px, start_px, width_tiles, class_id, lanes[], hatch | none}` in the template (LY-13). `pos_px` is `(line_px, start_px)` for E/W facings and `(start_px, line_px)` for N/S. The four-facing footprint, LOW-end, PLATE/JAMB/LEAF table of LY-13 is normative and is not restated.
- **States (TR-section-018, TR-assembly-025).** `FREE -> WELDED(seam_id) -> CAPPED` (after a SEALED cut) or `CUT_OPEN` (after a RAGGED cut); `CAPPED` and `CUT_OPEN` never return to `FREE` in MVP, which supports exactly one weld-then-cut cycle per socket. **A socket's state is written only inside LM2 and LM3.** There is no `install_cap_plate`, no `set_socket_state` and no setter on `LayoutState.sockets`; `socket_state` writes are private to `weld_math`/`detach_planner` helpers called by those two mutators, and a lint (`LAY-SOCKET-01`, tier E1, ADR-0010 § 6) rejects any other write to the `sockets` columns.
- **`can_attach` is a pure, first-failure-wins reason chain** (TR-section-019), cheap before expensive, in this fixed order: `SOCKET_UNKNOWN`, `SOCKET_NOT_FREE`, `SAME_BODY`, `FACING_MISMATCH`, `WIDTH_MISMATCH`, `CLASS_MISMATCH`, `LANE_MISMATCH`, `GEOM_OVERLAP`. `SAME_BODY` being a hard reject and every weld merging two bodies is what makes the weld relation a **forest** and a cut always split a body into exactly two components.
- **`GEOM_OVERLAP`.** The test set is the static footprint of both bodies after the D.6 translation: every static rect with all flags, each PLATE slot at its full footprint, no leaf and no JAMB slot, plus the tile cells of every room (rect against tile and tile against tile, so a wall over the other body's floor and two floors on one cell both fail); abutting is legal. It runs over each body's broadphase handle (ADR-0014) and is **memoised on `(socket_ref_a, socket_ref_b, static_version_a, static_version_b)`**; uncached cost target <= 2 ms (TR-section-019), a pending-spike figure (V3). The memo is a small fixed-capacity ring in `LayoutDerived`, reset on restore.
- **Slot activation is a pure function** of `(this socket's state, this socket's hatch, the mate's hatch, W)` evaluated by LM1 to LM4 and `post_restore` (the LY-15 matrix); no persisted field is needed because the mate's hatch is known from the two templates. A hatched socket whose mate is bare is `hatch_one_sided`: legal, behaves bulkhead-only, its PLATE stays on while `WELDED`.
- **The `can_attach` preview needs more than a reason**, and a Class A check returns a bare `StringName` (ADR-0003 § 5). So the payload `{reason, hatch_one_sided, openings_count}` is its own pure read, `preview_attach(socket_ref_a, socket_ref_b, out: AttachPreview) -> void`, and `can_attach(...)` is `preview_attach` followed by returning `out.reason` (`&""` = OK). One implementation, two shapes.
- **`socket_plan(socket_ref_a, socket_ref_b, out: WeldPlan)`** is a pure read that fills the Graph's weld-plan DATA verbatim (one lane pair per lane in `(loop, lane_index)` order, one opening per mated hatch pair `(comp_a, comp_b, area_max)`, `L_seam = width_tiles`). R("### 10. Dirty keys\n",
"""### 9.5 Layout port (`GraphLayoutAdapter`, CT-01, CT-03)

ADR-0013 § 8 owns `LayoutGraphPort` (`@abstract`, `src/sim/layout/ports/layout_graph_port.gd`) and the four caller-owned records it fills (`SectionBases`, `OpeningRead`, `SeamOpenings`, `SectionCounts`, `src/sim/layout/views/`). The adapter holds `GraphMutators` and `GraphView`, and only `GraphModule` and Layout hold the adapter, so ownership stays one-way (§ 6.3 Method C); `LayoutRoomSource` must in turn hold Layout's state and derived objects and not `LayoutModule`, or the mutual ports would close a reference cycle (the leak test covers the pair).

| Method | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `check_instantiate_section(views, section_id: int, template_id: String, kind: int) -> StringName` | the pure Class A check of M1 (`&""` = OK), the same function ADR-0012 calls `check_instantiate_section`: the LS-18 reasons plus `CAPACITY` (node, edge and `ID_MAX` slots, tombstones included) and `ONSET_UNKEYED` (`graph_rules.onset_valid`); Layout's `can_build` calls it |
| `instantiate_section(scope, section_id, template_id, kind, out: SectionBases) -> int` | M1 (§ 4.4): a status, the bases in `out` |
| `opening_into(edge_id: int, out: OpeningRead) -> bool` | false for a non-live or non-OPENING edge; else fills `area`, `area_max` and `door_state`, **derived from `area`** (LS-19) and never stored |
| `seam_openings_into(seam_id: int, out: SeamOpenings) -> bool` | false for an unknown seam; else `count` and `opening_ids` in `socket_plan.openings` order (the order `weld_join` appended them, § 4.1 (3)); **valid after restore**, because the lists are persisted (§ 3.6), and for a CUT record |
| `section_counts_into(section_id: int, out: SectionCounts) -> bool` | false for a section id the Graph has never held; else the counts of the rule below; reads **persisted columns only (Tier S)**, never a cache |

All five are allocation-free and write only into the caller-owned `out`. The three reads (`opening_into`, `seam_openings_into`, `section_counts_into`) are valid in APPLY, INIT, HOOK and `post_restore`; `check_instantiate_section` and `instantiate_section` are valid in APPLY and INIT (the INIT pass is stamped at the N2 clock, ADR-0012 § 5).

**`section_counts_into` and RAGGED stubs (CT-03).** It fills `nodes`, `edges` and `comps` with the **template-range** counts: the node rows in `[node_base, node_base + template.node_count)`, the matching edge range M1 created for this section, and the compartments `comp_base + k`. It fills `stub_count` with the STUB rows a RAGGED `cut_detach` created (§ 3.6): a stub's `section_of` is the cut section, and stubs, appended with fresh high ids, lie **outside** the template range, as do seam edges. It sets `tombstoned` true when every template-range row of the section is tombstoned (a discarded section), and fills `next_section_id` from `hdr`. Layout's `post_restore` check (d) therefore compares template-range rows only (ADR-0013 § 10); stubs resolve through `GraphView.section_of(id)` plus the seam's `stub_ids`, and `anchor_geometry(stub)` answers the cut socket's hatch span (ADR-0013 § 3, § 11). Without this definition every save made after a RAGGED cut would fail that check.

### 10. Dirty keys
""")

# 12.1
d.repline("**12.1 The writer-file rule (TR-lsg-002).**",
  """**12.1 The writer matrix (TR-lsg-002, CT-07).** The persisted columns are underscore-prefixed members of `GraphState` (`_n_hp`, `_e_hp`, `_c_n_o2`, ...; prefix per table: `_n_`, `_p_`, `_e_`, `_c_`, `_m_` seams, `_x_` sections, `_q_` queues, `_d_` defs, `_h_` header). Writers are named per class and, where a member needs more than the class default, per member. Explicit per-member writer files were chosen over routing every cache write through `GraphDerived`, because the last-emitted bucket update happens on every mark in hot code and an extra call per mark is the wrong place to spend budget.

| Class | Members | Writer files (`src/sim/graph/`) |
|---|---|---|
| `GraphState` | every member | `propagate/**`, `graph_mutators.gd`, `graph_restore.gd` |
| `GraphCaches` | every member | `graph_derived.gd` |
| `GraphCaches` | the intensive values (`P`, `p_o2`, `o2_pm`, trend), the descriptor store and `alarm_sections` | also `propagate/**` (ADR-0012 phases 0, 7 and 11) |
| `GraphCaches` | the last-emitted buckets | also `propagate/**` and `graph_mutators.gd` (updated at every mark, whoever marked it) |
| `GraphScratch` | contents (accumulators, island, candidate and sort buffers) | `propagate/**`; also `graph_derived.gd` for the two traversal buffers `stack` and `queue` that `ensure_derived` uses (ADR-0012 § 4) |
| `GraphScratch` | sizing (`resize`, ADR-0012's `size_scratch()`) | `graph_derived.gd` |
| `GraphDiag` | every member | any Graph file |

`propagate/**` is ADR-0012's directory (the dispatcher `graph_propagate.gd` and one file per phase). **Reader files** are `graph_snapshot.gd`, `views/graph_view.gd`, `views/graph_view_cold.gd`, `graph_layout_adapter.gd` and `graph_invariants.gd`; reads of a prefixed member through a foreign receiver elsewhere are findings. **ADR-0010 has no rule that expresses this, and ARCH-06 (registry `foreign_private_member_access`) forbids the very `state._n_hp[i] = v` access the writers need.** Foundation ask 1: a config-driven rule, `OWN-01`, reading `tools/lint/config/field_writers.json` (`{class, member_prefix, members, writer_files, reader_files}`, where `writer_files` entries are files or directory globs and `members` carries the per-member entries), which (a) exempts the listed writer and reader files from ARCH-06 for that class's prefix, (b) flags any assignment, compound assignment or mutating call (`resize`, `fill`, `set`, `append`, `push_back`, `insert`, `remove_at`, `sort`, `reverse`, `append_array`) on a member with that prefix in any other file, and (c) flags a `static var` in the four class files (§ 6.3 Method C). This absorbs ADR-0012's Foundation Ask 1. It is a lexical rule at file granularity (ADR-0010 accepts that field-writer rules are weaker than an AST would make them, OQ-J); the reflection test of § 6.3 and the per-mutator key test are the runtime backstop. ADR-0012's Key Interfaces comment cites this section instead of restating the set.""")
R("### Architecture Diagram",
"""**12.3 Adopted from ADR-0012.** Members and constants this ADR carries because ADR-0012's design needs them: `GraphIds.ALARM_CAPABLE_MASK`; `GraphTuning` fields `hook_offset_power/atmo/failure`, `load_queue_max`, `w_min_steps`, the `burst_*` fields and the `rate_pm` inputs (`derelict_fault_compression`), with the RNG id-field relation checked by `GRAPH_BOOT_TUNING`; `GraphCaches` members `active_nodes`, `active_edges`, `active_comps`, `active_seams`, `store_slots`, `machine_slots`, `exchange_links`, the POWER island list, `alarm_sections` and the sizing functions `size_derived()`, `size_scratch()`, `size_descriptors()` (bodies in `graph_derived.gd`); `GraphDiag` counters `late_rebuilds`, `queue_dropped`, `footprints_clamped` (and `schedule_shift`, § 7.4); the `ONSET_UNKEYED` reason of the M1 check (§ 9.5); and `FailureFilter.loaded_only`, retained for type stability and always satisfied (§ 9.4). `derived_members.json` lists every non-persisted member named here.

### Architecture Diagram""")

  "- **Rejection Reason**: LS-1 (c) and TR-lsg-004 for the intensive atmosphere values only (`P`, `p_o2`, `o2_pm`, trend): they are pure functions of `n`, `V` and `p_prev`, the derived cache is rebuilt eagerly (at the end of phase 7, at the end of phase 0 and in `post_restore`), so the reads are already O(1) and a restore rebuilds them exactly. ### Key Interfaces

```gdscript
class_name ModuleFacet extends RefCounted            # what a simulation module gets in setup() (ADR-0001)
var registrar: BlockRegistrar                         # BOOTING only; set to null at the freeze
var views: SimViews                                   # kept after the freeze
var fault_domain: int                                 # the module's static DOMAIN_ID
var rng: RngFacet                                     # null when the module declares no RNG streams (ADR-0005 § 2.3)
var clock: ClockView                                  # read-only (T, world_seed, restore_epoch); see § 10
# Other owners' published mutator objects are wired by the composition root into the module's
# own setup() arguments (for example Assembly receives Graph, Layout, Body and Interaction).
137:**Construction and injection (resolves the setup cycle).** `LayoutViews` extends `RefCounted` only (GDScript has single inheritance, so it cannot extend several ports). It is constructed inside `LayoutModule.setup(facet, templates, tuning)` and lives for the whole process. Each port is satisfied by a small adapter that delegates to it, with the port's method names: `LayoutRoomSource extends RoomSource` (`room_volume_tiles` wraps `V`, `room_exposed_tiles` wraps `exposed_tiles`, both return -1 for an unknown room), `LayoutSolidQuery extends SolidQuery` and `LayoutOccluderSource extends OccluderSource` (ADR-0014). The composition root (a) calls `LayoutModule.setup` (no Graph argument), (b) passes `layout.room_source()` to `GraphModule.setup(facet, tuning, catalog, rooms, strict_numeric)`, (c) calls `LayoutModule.bind_graph(port: LayoutGraphPort)` with `graph.layout_port()` after `GraphModule.setup` and **before the registry freeze**. A port call made before `bind_graph` is an asserted defect. The `architecture.md` § 8 step 4 note is updated accordingly (routed to `/architecture-review`).
211:- **The record (TR-section-010).** A rect is `(x0, y0, x1, y1)` in section-local base px, **half-open** `[x0, x1) x [y0, y1)` over pixel cells, with one flags byte: `SOLID`, `OCCLUDES_LIGHT`, `DOOR_LEAF`, `PROP`, `MACHINE`, `HULL` (registry `layout_rect_flags`); the bit values and the `ALL` mask live in `src/sim/layout/rect_flags.gd` (`RectFlags`), which ADR-0014 and ADR-0034 import. The legal flag combinations are LY-7's table and a boot error otherwise (`RECT_FLAGS_ILLEGAL`). A rect with `x1 <= x0` or `y1 <= y0` is omitted from every result but keeps its `idx`.
397:func bind_graph(port: LayoutGraphPort) -> void                    # after GraphModule.setup, before the registry freeze; a port call earlier is an asserted defect
504:- **Must** call `bind_graph` before the registry freeze and make every port call after it; **must** implement `RoomSource` through `LayoutRoomSource`; **must never** extend more than one port from one class.

registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- fault_domain_table (state_ownership, ADR-0003): add docs/architecture/adr-0011-life-support-graph-data-model.md (domain 3 local code list written here)
- block_persistence_payload (interfaces, ADR-0006): add this ADR (nested String-keyed Dictionary of duplicated columns; restore precedence)
- dirty_key_encoding (api_decisions, ADR-0004): add this ADR (Graph kinds and the L/ and F/ packing)

- packed_array_exposed_or_setter_tracked (forbidden_patterns, ADR-0010): add this ADR (alarm_sections and failures use caller-owned buffers)
- integer_division_convention (api_decisions, ADR-0005): add this ADR (no file-level ignore in src/sim/graph)

gdd_sync.old: each file of `src/sim/graph/` opens with `@warning_ignore_start("integer_division")`, because every flux division is intentional integer division and would otherwise flood the editor with warnings; S0-b verifies that this annotation exists in 4.7.2 and silences the warning
gdd_sync.new: no file in `src/sim/graph/` carries an `integer_division` ignore: every division goes through `IntMath.floor_div`/`ceil_div`/`trunc_div` (ADR-0005 section 1.4; ADR-0010 SIM-04/SIM-05 allow exactly one ignore, in `IntMath.trunc_div`); S0-b no longer verifies the annotation (ADR-0011 section 2.3)

gdd_sync.old: every field is underscore-prefixed and a lint forbids writes outside the four writer files `graph_mutators.gd`, `graph_propagate.gd`, `graph_restore.gd` (decode, validate, swap) and `graph_derived.gd` (non-persisted caches only)
gdd_sync.new: every persisted column of `GraphState` is underscore-prefixed and written only in the `propagate/` directory, `graph_mutators.gd` and `graph_restore.gd`; derived caches, scratch buffers and diagnostics are the separate classes `GraphCaches` (written by `graph_derived.gd`, plus the propagate directory for the intensive values, descriptor store and alarm list, and the propagate directory and `graph_mutators.gd` for the last-emitted buckets), `GraphScratch` (contents in the propagate directory, sizing in `graph_derived.gd`) and `GraphDiag` (any Graph file), and the DERIVED allowlist of the reflection test is the member list of those classes (ADR-0011 sections 1, 6.3, 12.1)

gdd_sync.old: Every check is raised through `GraphFault.raise(code, subject)`, which records the code, returns the failure to the kernel and, in debug, also halts
gdd_sync.new: Every check is raised through `GraphFault.raise_in(scope, code, subject)` (or `raise_ctx(ctx, code, subject, detail)` in restore and post_restore, which never writes to the caller's `detail`), which faults the scope or context with a domain-3 code and returns -code; the debug halt is the kernel's FAULTED dev rule (ADR-0011 section 8.2)

gdd_sync.old: a numeric *soft* violation in play is a *hard* failure on load, because a corrupt save must not be "fixed" into a different world
gdd_sync.new: a numeric soft violation in play is a hard failure on load against the physical ceilings in `GraphTuning`; a store above a lowered live catalog `stock_cap` is not a violation: it restores exactly and the first phase 0 clamps it, credits `discarded_*`, counts `stock_clamped` (not a saturation) and emits a diagnostic (ADR-0011 section 7.3; TR-itemdb-033)

gdd_sync.old: Instruments' `load = ⌊1000 × demand / max(1, supply)⌋` is its own reading, not `ρ`, and reads no `cap`
gdd_sync.new: the Graph publishes `true_value(LOAD_PM)` = 0 when `supply` is 0, else `min(1250, floor(1000 × demand / supply))`, with dead/idle/overload cases from `power_component_case`; Instruments reads it and derives nothing (ADR-0011 section 9.2; TR-instr-027)

gdd_sync.old: `alarm_sections()` → ascending, duplicate-free `section_id`s
gdd_sync.new: `alarm_sections(out: PackedInt32Array) -> int` fills a caller-owned buffer with ascending, duplicate-free `section_id`s and returns the count; the other list queries (`nodes_in`, `neighbors`, `open_ends`, `hull_segments_of`, `compartments_in_section`) use caller-owned buffers the same way; `step_no()` is `floor_div(T, GRAPH_STEP_TICKS)`; a non-live id reads as the documented sentinel (`node_state` and `edge_state` return -1, not the healthy 0) and `node_live`/`edge_live`/`compartment_live` are the guards (ADR-0011 section 9.1)

gdd_sync.old: (the packing and its range check are fixed by ADR-0011)
gdd_sync.new: composite packing is `(loop << 24) | anchor` with the anchor below `ID_MAX` 2^24; `F/<id>` is the DESC kind keyed per subject as `(subject_kind << 28) | subject_id`; `N/<id>` is the family of both the NODE and EDGE kinds (ADR-0011 section 10)

gdd_sync.old: | `cause` | ENDOGENOUS 0 / EXOGENOUS 1 | Last damage cause tag on the subject |
gdd_sync.new: | `cause` | ENDOGENOUS 0 / EXOGENOUS 1 | Last damage cause tag on the subject; persisted as the EXOGENOUS flag bit of the node/edge `flags` column (ADR-0011 section 3.2)

gdd_sync.old: `discarded_*`, `withdrawn_*` (M16, per medium)
gdd_sync.new: `discarded_*`, `withdrawn_*` (M16, per medium: gas mGU, coolant mL, fuel mL, energy dJ; sixteen int64 counters per section with the eight named above, ADR-0011 section 3.7)

gdd_sync.old: `EMPTY` (`default_state()`: no sections, counters at 1, `last_step_no` 0)
gdd_sync.new: `EMPTY` (`default_state()`: the EXTERIOR node row (id 0, section 0), no sections, counters at 1, `last_step_no` and the power-use window 0, the schedule in force taken from the live tuning; built as a payload that the Graph's own `restore` accepts, ADR-0011 section 4.6)

gdd_sync.old: a virtual hole of `A_CUT` 24 is attached to each side's compartment as a hull stub with `hp` 2500
gdd_sync.new: a hull stub with `hp` 2500 and `A_CUT` 24 is attached to each side's compartment; each stub is an appended HULL_SEGMENT node row (flag STUB, fresh high id outside the section's contiguous M1 range) listed in the SeamRecord's `stub_ids`, so no new persisted record type exists (ADR-0011 sections 3.6, 9.5)

gdd_sync.old: `instantiate_section` → `{node_base, edge_base, comp_base}`
gdd_sync.new: `instantiate_section` → `SectionBases {node_base, edge_base, comp_base}` (ADR-0013's record); M1's only caller is Layout LM1 through `LayoutGraphPort`, and its check carries `ONSET_UNKEYED`: node ids are allocated contiguously in template order with COMPARTMENT nodes first, so `comp_base == node_base` and `cid(room k) == comp_base + k`; `section_id` 0 is reserved for EXTERIOR (ADR-0011 sections 4.4, 9.5)

gdd_sync.old: `served_pm` is not, because phase 2 recomputes it before use
gdd_sync.new: `served_pm` is also persisted, as the hook product `n_served`, together with `n_draw`, the CABLE net load (edge `e0`) and the five-step `power_use` window, because a restore between the power hook and the atmo or failure hook cannot rebuild them from post-phase state (ADR-0011 sections 3.2, 3.4, 3.8, 6.1; ADR-0012 section 11)

gdd_sync.old: id → slot maps, `served_pm`, descriptors, `P`/`p_o2`/`o2_pm`, last-emitted buckets, the cached hash
gdd_sync.new: id → slot maps, descriptors, `P`/`p_o2`/`o2_pm`/trend, last-emitted buckets, the cached hash (`served_pm` is read from the persisted `n_served`)

gdd_sync.old: `P`, `p_o2`, `o2_pm`, `served_pm`, `circ`, every descriptor and every cache are derived on read or in the run and never persisted
gdd_sync.new: `P`, `p_o2`, `o2_pm`, `circ`, every descriptor and every cache are derived on read or in the run and never persisted; `served_pm` is read from the persisted hook product `n_served` (with `n_draw`, the CABLE net load and the power-use window; ADR-0011 sections 3.2, 6.1)

gdd_sync.old: Extensive quantities are stored and intensive ones (P, p_o2, served_pm, descriptors) are derived on read; only hysteresis memory (band_o2/p/t, p_prev, SEAL_STRAIN bits) and warn trackers are persisted.
gdd_sync.new: Extensive quantities are stored and intensive ones (P, p_o2, o2_pm, descriptors) are derived on read; persisted are the hysteresis memory (band_o2/p/t, p_prev, SEAL_STRAIN bits), the warn trackers and the phase-2 hook products (n_served, n_draw, CABLE net load, power_use window).

gdd_sync.old: spawns, despawns and re-selects size and behaviour on `F/` and `N/`
gdd_sync.new: spawns, despawns and re-selects size and behaviour on `F/` (the Graph's DESC kind, one key per subject) and `N/` (the Graph's NODE and EDGE kinds)

decisions.chosen: Option (i): explicit per-member writer files (a matrix per class in 12.1), not routing every cache write through GraphDerived
decisions.reason: Last-emitted bucket updates happen on every mark in hot code; an extra call per mark is the wrong place to spend budget (the CT-07 ruling).

decisions.chosen: Pre-commit lever 1 (fluid-stamp side table) now and keep 3.2/3.4 listing the pre-lever stamps; the lifetime-worst fixture decides whether lever 3 (raised ceiling) is requested
decisions.reason: The lifetime-worst state cannot be measured here; row arithmetic suggests about 0.6-0.8 KB per RAGGED-cycled socket, so the ceiling is plausibly passed. The exact fstamps column layout is deliberately deferred to the schema commit, since no save exists yet.

decisions.chosen: GraphLimits.TEMP_NONE (-(1<<30)) instead of CT-09/T6's -1; other compartment getters return -1
decisions.reason: -1 mC is a legal temperature, so -1 would be a value inside the domain; pressure, partial pressure, o2_pm, bands and trend are non-negative.

decisions.chosen: Added compartment_live(cid) alongside node_live/edge_live
decisions.reason: Compartment getters have the same ambiguity and the guard costs one O(1) getter.

decisions.chosen: graph_derived.gd also writes the scratch stack/queue buffers that ensure_derived uses, in addition to sizing
decisions.reason: ADR-0012 4 places the BFS buffers in GraphScratch and calls them from ensure_derived; without this the OWN-01 matrix would flag legal code.

decisions.chosen: Deleted, not aliased; ADR-0013's SectionBases is the only M1 out record
decisions.reason: CT-01: an alias keeps two names for one record.

decisions.chosen: GraphLayoutAdapter in src/sim/graph/graph_layout_adapter.gd, outside ports/
decisions.reason: ADR-0010 ARCH-05 requires every file under ports/ to be @abstract; GraphView must stay getter-only and GraphModule cannot inherit twice.

decisions.chosen: setup(facet, tuning, catalog, rooms, strict_numeric, work) with facet.clock as the ClockView source; setup constructs the single GraphView and the adapter, and read_view puts that same view
decisions.reason: ADR-0003 10 puts clock on ModuleFacet; ADR-0012 only adds a trailing WorkCounter; ADR-0013 calls setup with the same shape; avoids the construction-order conflict with read_view at the registry freeze.

decisions.chosen: Seventeen individual _h_* int members (power_use_w0..w4 collectively power_use_w5; sched_div and sched_off_power/atmo/failure collectively sched); snapshot builds the hdr Dictionary
decisions.reason: Header values must be ints; the collective names let ADR-0012/ADR-0016 keep the names used in the rulings.

decisions.chosen: HOOK_CURSOR is local 25 (runtime, ADR-0012) and RESTORE_HOOK_CURSOR is local 26 (7.2 step 13), checked against the sched stored in the payload
decisions.reason: CT-08: 25 collides with the runtime code; ADR-0016 4.4 forbids asserting a catalogue tunable at restore, so the comparison uses stored offsets.

decisions.chosen: About 30.5 KB (29,674 + 840 + 40) against 32,000 bytes, 4.6 percent headroom, about 4.2 percent with the four sched ints; ceiling near 111 nodes / 159 edges
decisions.reason: CT-04 gave 30.5 KB; sched (CT-08) adds about 100 bytes not counted there; 32 KB is used as 32,000 bytes as in ADR-0012.

open_questions: fstamps side table: lever 1 is pre-committed but its column layout, fluid-subject predicate and id-to-row map are unspecified, so GraphSchema v1 cannot be written from the text alone; the schema commit that introduces it must also update sections 3.2 and 3.4 and the fingerprint (owner: this ADR's first schema story).

Lifetime-worst snapshot fixture (every socket welded and cut RAGGED once, queues at bound, maximal defs) is unmeasured; if it exceeds 32,000 bytes after lever 1, a raised TR-lsg-036 ceiling must be requested from ADR-0012 (pending S3).

Cross-ADR ask to ADR-0013: LayoutRoomSource and the Layout state it wraps must hold state/derived objects, not LayoutModule, or the mutual ports (Layout holds the Graph adapter, Graph holds LayoutRoomSource) close a RefCounted cycle; ADR-0013 should state the rule and join the leak test.

ADR-0016 still owes the alignments of CT-08/CT-10: kernel.clock (T, world_seed) as Tier S from R2, V3 reworded to the thirteen ordered steps of 7.2, V7 decoding with GraphView.step_no(), and the KRN-RST-12 corrupt-cursor fixture row.

registry_candidates.name: existing entries gaining ADR-0011
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- fault_domain_table (state_ownership, ADR-0003): add docs/architecture/adr-0011-life-support-graph-data-model.md (domain 3 local code list written here)
- block_persistence_payload (interfaces, ADR-0006): add this ADR (nested String-keyed Dictionary of duplicated columns; restore precedence)
- dirty_key_encoding (api_decisions, ADR-0004): add this ADR (Graph kinds and the L/ and F/ packing)
- id_ledgers (state_ownership, ADR-0007): add this ADR (graph ids.lock.json spaces)
- foreign_private_member_access (forbidden_patterns, ADR-0010): add this ADR (writer/reader file exemption request, with directory globs and per-member entries)
- packed_array_exposed_or_setter_tracked (forbidden_patterns, ADR-0010): add this ADR (alarm_sections and failures use caller-owned buffers)
- integer_division_convention (api_decisions, ADR-0005): add this ADR (no file-level ignore in src/sim/graph)

gdd_sync.old: each file of `src/sim/graph/` opens with `@warning_ignore_start("integer_division")`, because every flux division is intentional integer division and would otherwise flood the editor with warnings; S0-b verifies that this annotation exists in 4.7.2 and silences the warning
gdd_sync.new: no file in `src/sim/graph/` carries an `integer_division` ignore: every division goes through `IntMath.floor_div`/`ceil_div`/`trunc_div` (ADR-0005 section 1.4; ADR-0010 SIM-04/SIM-05 allow exactly one ignore, in `IntMath.trunc_div`); S0-b no longer verifies the annotation (ADR-0011 section 2.3)

gdd_sync.old: every field is underscore-prefixed and a lint forbids writes outside the four writer files `graph_mutators.gd`, `graph_propagate.gd`, `graph_restore.gd` (decode, validate, swap) and `graph_derived.gd` (non-persisted caches only)
gdd_sync.new: every persisted column of `GraphState` is underscore-prefixed and written only in the `propagate/` directory, `graph_mutators.gd` and `graph_restore.gd`; derived caches, scratch buffers and diagnostics are the separate classes `GraphCaches` (written by `graph_derived.gd`, plus the propagate directory for the intensive values, descriptor store and alarm list, and the propagate directory and `graph_mutators.gd` for the last-emitted buckets), `GraphScratch` (contents in the propagate directory, sizing in `graph_derived.gd`) and `GraphDiag` (any Graph file), and the DERIVED allowlist of the reflection test is the member list of those classes (ADR-0011 sections 1, 6.3, 12.1)

gdd_sync.old: Every check is raised through `GraphFault.raise(code, subject)`, which records the code, returns the failure to the kernel and, in debug, also halts
gdd_sync.new: Every check is raised through `GraphFault.raise_in(scope, code, subject)` (or `raise_ctx(ctx, code, subject, detail)` in restore and post_restore, which never writes to the caller's `detail`), which faults the scope or context with a domain-3 code and returns -code; the debug halt is the kernel's FAULTED dev rule (ADR-0011 section 8.2)

gdd_sync.old: a numeric *soft* violation in play is a *hard* failure on load, because a corrupt save must not be "fixed" into a different world
gdd_sync.new: a numeric soft violation in play is a hard failure on load against the physical ceilings in `GraphTuning`; a store above a lowered live catalog `stock_cap` is not a violation: it restores exactly and the first phase 0 clamps it, credits `discarded_*`, counts `stock_clamped` (not a saturation) and emits a diagnostic (ADR-0011 section 7.3; TR-itemdb-033)

gdd_sync.old: Instruments' `load = ⌊1000 × demand / max(1, supply)⌋` is its own reading, not `ρ`, and reads no `cap`
gdd_sync.new: the Graph publishes `true_value(LOAD_PM)` = 0 when `supply` is 0, else `min(1250, floor(1000 × demand / supply))`, with dead/idle/overload cases from `power_component_case`; Instruments reads it and derives nothing (ADR-0011 section 9.2; TR-instr-027)

gdd_sync.old: `alarm_sections()` → ascending, duplicate-free `section_id`s
gdd_sync.new: `alarm_sections(out: PackedInt32Array) -> int` fills a caller-owned buffer with ascending, duplicate-free `section_id`s and returns the count; the other list queries (`nodes_in`, `neighbors`, `open_ends`, `hull_segments_of`, `compartments_in_section`) use caller-owned buffers the same way; `step_no()` is `floor_div(T, GRAPH_STEP_TICKS)`; a non-live id reads as the documented sentinel (`node_state` and `edge_state` return -1, not the healthy 0) and `node_live`/`edge_live`/`compartment_live` are the guards (ADR-0011 section 9.1)

gdd_sync.old: (the packing and its range check are fixed by ADR-0011)
gdd_sync.new: composite packing is `(loop << 24) | anchor` with the anchor below `ID_MAX` 2^24; `F/<id>` is the DESC kind keyed per subject as `(subject_kind << 28) | subject_id`; `N/<id>` is the family of both the NODE and EDGE kinds (ADR-0011 section 10)

gdd_sync.old: | `cause` | ENDOGENOUS 0 / EXOGENOUS 1 | Last damage cause tag on the subject |
gdd_sync.new: | `cause` | ENDOGENOUS 0 / EXOGENOUS 1 | Last damage cause tag on the subject; persisted as the EXOGENOUS flag bit of the node/edge `flags` column (ADR-0011 section 3.2)

gdd_sync.old: `discarded_*`, `withdrawn_*` (M16, per medium)
gdd_sync.new: `discarded_*`, `withdrawn_*` (M16, per medium: gas mGU, coolant mL, fuel mL, energy dJ; sixteen int64 counters per section with the eight named above, ADR-0011 section 3.7)

gdd_sync.old: `EMPTY` (`default_state()`: no sections, counters at 1, `last_step_no` 0)
gdd_sync.new: `EMPTY` (`default_state()`: the EXTERIOR node row (id 0, section 0), no sections, counters at 1, `last_step_no` and the power-use window 0, the schedule in force taken from the live tuning; built as a payload that the Graph's own `restore` accepts, ADR-0011 section 4.6)

gdd_sync.old: a virtual hole of `A_CUT` 24 is attached to each side's compartment as a hull stub with `hp` 2500
gdd_sync.new: a hull stub with `hp` 2500 and `A_CUT` 24 is attached to each side's compartment; each stub is an appended HULL_SEGMENT node row (flag STUB, fresh high id outside the section's contiguous M1 range) listed in the SeamRecord's `stub_ids`, so no new persisted record type exists (ADR-0011 sections 3.6, 9.5)

gdd_sync.old: `instantiate_section` → `{node_base, edge_base, comp_base}`
gdd_sync.new: `instantiate_section` → `SectionBases {node_base, edge_base, comp_base}` (ADR-0013's record); M1's only caller is Layout LM1 through `LayoutGraphPort`, and its check carries `ONSET_UNKEYED`: node ids are allocated contiguously in template order with COMPARTMENT nodes first, so `comp_base == node_base` and `cid(room k) == comp_base + k`; `section_id` 0 is reserved for EXTERIOR (ADR-0011 sections 4.4, 9.5)

gdd_sync.old: `served_pm` is not, because phase 2 recomputes it before use
gdd_sync.new: `served_pm` is also persisted, as the hook product `n_served`, together with `n_draw`, the CABLE net load (edge `e0`) and the five-step `power_use` window, because a restore between the power hook and the atmo or failure hook cannot rebuild them from post-phase state (ADR-0011 sections 3.2, 3.4, 3.8, 6.1; ADR-0012 section 11)

gdd_sync.old: id → slot maps, `served_pm`, descriptors, `P`/`p_o2`/`o2_pm`, last-emitted buckets, the cached hash
gdd_sync.new: id → slot maps, descriptors, `P`/`p_o2`/`o2_pm`/trend, last-emitted buckets, the cached hash (`served_pm` is read from the persisted `n_served`)

gdd_sync.old: `P`, `p_o2`, `o2_pm`, `served_pm`, `circ`, every descriptor and every cache are derived on read or in the run and never persisted
gdd_sync.new: `P`, `p_o2`, `o2_pm`, `circ`, every descriptor and every cache are derived on read or in the run and never persisted; `served_pm` is read from the persisted hook product `n_served` (with `n_draw`, the CABLE net load and the power-use window; ADR-0011 sections 3.2, 6.1)

gdd_sync.old: Extensive quantities are stored and intensive ones (P, p_o2, served_pm, descriptors) are derived on read; only hysteresis memory (band_o2/p/t, p_prev, SEAL_STRAIN bits) and warn trackers are persisted.
gdd_sync.new: Extensive quantities are stored and intensive ones (P, p_o2, o2_pm, descriptors) are derived on read; persisted are the hysteresis memory (band_o2/p/t, p_prev, SEAL_STRAIN bits), the warn trackers and the phase-2 hook products (n_served, n_draw, CABLE net load, power_use window).

gdd_sync.old: spawns, despawns and re-selects size and behaviour on `F/` and `N/`
gdd_sync.new: spawns, despawns and re-selects size and behaviour on `F/` (the Graph's DESC kind, one key per subject) and `N/` (the Graph's NODE and EDGE kinds)

decisions.chosen: Option (i): explicit per-member writer files (a matrix per class in 12.1), not routing every cache write through GraphDerived
decisions.reason: Last-emitted bucket updates happen on every mark in hot code; an extra call per mark is the wrong place to spend budget (the CT-07 ruling).

decisions.chosen: Pre-commit lever 1 (fluid-stamp side table) now and keep 3.2/3.4 listing the pre-lever stamps; the lifetime-worst fixture decides whether lever 3 (raised ceiling) is requested
decisions.reason: The lifetime-worst state cannot be measured here; row arithmetic suggests about 0.6-0.8 KB per RAGGED-cycled socket, so the ceiling is plausibly passed. The exact fstamps column layout is deliberately deferred to the schema commit, since no save exists yet.

decisions.chosen: GraphLimits.TEMP_NONE (-(1<<30)) instead of CT-09/T6's -1; other compartment getters return -1
decisions.reason: -1 mC is a legal temperature, so -1 would be a value inside the domain; pressure, partial pressure, o2_pm, bands and trend are non-negative.

decisions.chosen: Added compartment_live(cid) alongside node_live/edge_live
decisions.reason: Compartment getters have the same ambiguity and the guard costs one O(1) getter.

decisions.chosen: graph_derived.gd also writes the scratch stack/queue buffers that ensure_derived uses, in addition to sizing
decisions.reason: ADR-0012 4 places the BFS buffers in GraphScratch and calls them from ensure_derived; without this the OWN-01 matrix would flag legal code.

decisions.chosen: Deleted, not aliased; ADR-0013's SectionBases is the only M1 out record
decisions.reason: CT-01: an alias keeps two names for one record.

decisions.chosen: GraphLayoutAdapter in src/sim/graph/graph_layout_adapter.gd, outside ports/
decisions.reason: ADR-0010 ARCH-05 requires every file under ports/ to be @abstract; GraphView must stay getter-only and GraphModule cannot inherit twice.

decisions.chosen: setup(facet, tuning, catalog, rooms, strict_numeric, work) with facet.clock as the ClockView source; setup constructs the single GraphView and the adapter, and read_view puts that same view
decisions.reason: ADR-0003 10 puts clock on ModuleFacet; ADR-0012 only adds a trailing WorkCounter; ADR-0013 calls setup with the same shape; avoids the construction-order conflict with read_view at the registry freeze.

decisions.chosen: Seventeen individual _h_* int members (power_use_w0..w4 collectively power_use_w5; sched_div and sched_off_power/atmo/failure collectively sched); snapshot builds the hdr Dictionary
decisions.reason: Header values must be ints; the collective names let ADR-0012/ADR-0016 keep the names used in the rulings.

decisions.chosen: HOOK_CURSOR is local 25 (runtime, ADR-0012) and RESTORE_HOOK_CURSOR is local 26 (7.2 step 13), checked against the sched stored in the payload
decisions.reason: CT-08: 25 collides with the runtime code; ADR-0016 4.4 forbids asserting a catalogue tunable at restore, so the comparison uses stored offsets.

decisions.chosen: About 30.5 KB (29,674 + 840 + 40) against 32,000 bytes, 4.6 percent headroom, about 4.2 percent with the four sched ints; ceiling near 111 nodes / 159 edges
decisions.reason: CT-04 gave 30.5 KB; sched (CT-08) adds about 100 bytes not counted there; 32 KB is used as 32,000 bytes as in ADR-0012.

open_questions: fstamps side table: lever 1 is pre-committed but its column layout, fluid-subject predicate and id-to-row map are unspecified, so GraphSchema v1 cannot be written from the text alone; the schema commit that introduces it must also update sections 3.2 and 3.4 and the fingerprint (owner: this ADR's first schema story).

Lifetime-worst snapshot fixture (every socket welded and cut RAGGED once, queues at bound, maximal defs) is unmeasured; if it exceeds 32,000 bytes after lever 1, a raised TR-lsg-036 ceiling must be requested from ADR-0012 (pending S3).

Cross-ADR ask to ADR-0013: LayoutRoomSource and the Layout state it wraps must hold state/derived objects, not LayoutModule, or the mutual ports (Layout holds the Graph adapter, Graph holds LayoutRoomSource) close a RefCounted cycle; ADR-0013 should state the rule and join the leak test.

ADR-0016 still owes the alignments of CT-08/CT-10: kernel.clock (T, world_seed) as Tier S from R2, V3 reworded to the thirteen ordered steps of 7.2, V7 decoding with GraphView.step_no(), and the KRN-RST-12 corrupt-cursor fixture row.

ADR-0012 still owes the retargeting of its cursor cross-ADR note to ADR-0011 7.2 step 13, the deletion of its 'if ADR-0011 declines' text in section 11, and restoring the power_use window from power_use_w5; ADR-0017 should cite node_live/edge_live by name (D3/D5).

Registry/GDD gaps unchanged: LOAD_QUANTUM_PERMILLE is absent from entities.yaml; pending-load bound, JOIN_PAIRS_MAX, JOIN_OPENINGS_MAX, max_stock_gas and max_stock_liquid remain placeholders (Open Questions 5 and 6); S1 may still require an ADR-0010 amendment for inlined non-negative division (Open Question 1).

applied: T1/CT-04 persisted hook products n_served, n_draw, CABLE e0 net load, power_use window (collectively power_use_w5), size figures, Alternative 7, derived_members description, Open Question 2 closed
T2/CT-05 hdr.last_step_no is the last step whose failure hook completed (2.3, 3.8, GraphView.last_step_no doc)
